title: Kafka vs Pulsar-class vs Kinesis-class vs DB outbox-only
description: Pick a log or skip the log from access pattern and the durability envelope you can name. TokenX money is the ledger, not the topic.

cells.workload: Durable append-only facts, independent consumer groups, replay inside retention, partition-key order. TokenX settlement commands and Ad Click billed facts after an outbox or collector append.
cells.consistency: Append order per partition, not event-time. At-least-once to consumers unless you name a produce-plus-offset transaction boundary. Offsets are group progress, not ledger proof. Not a linearizable money store.
cells.latency: Produce p50 often low-ms in-region after ISR ack. Consume lag is HW minus applied offset. Page-cache append is not an fsync certificate.
cells.scaling: Partitions cap one group's parallelism. Hot keys pin one partition. Add partitions only as a key-mapping change.
cells.failure: ISR shrink vs minISR=2 rejects writes. Unclean election can drop acknowledged offsets. Retention deletes. Consumer lag and dual-owner rebalance are independent of broker failover.
cells.costOps: You run brokers, disks, ISR, controller/KRaft, retention, consumer groups, DLQ ownership. Replication bytes ≈ produce × RF.
cells.whenNot: When the only consumer is a couple of workers on the primary, or you cannot staff RF=3 / acks=all / minISR=2 / ISR-only election. Do not treat the log as TokenX balances.

cells.workload: Multi-tenant topics, many independent subscriptions (cursors) per topic, optional segment offload to object storage, geo-replication as a named cluster feature.
cells.consistency: Per-partition (bundle) append order. Each subscription has its own cursor. Still at-least-once at external sinks. Segmented storage does not make event-time order. Not TokenX conservation.
cells.latency: Produce waits on bookie ack-quorum, not Kafka ISR by that name. Catch-up can read sealed segments/object offload instead of one broker's whole partition file.
cells.scaling: Brokers (compute/serving) and bookies (durable segments) scale on different axes. Bundles split for topic load.
cells.failure: Ack-quorum not met rejects the write. Bookie loss is a storage-plane failure; broker loss is a serving-plane failure; metadata store loss is a third plane. Name ensemble / write quorum / ack quorum.
cells.costOps: Two storage planes plus metadata. BookKeeper disks, offload, and tenant quotas. Operational surface is larger than a small Kafka cluster.
cells.whenNot: A small team that cannot staff brokers + bookies + metadata. Spendable balances as a Pulsar topic. Assuming geo-replication is a synchronous ledger.

cells.workload: AWS-centric ingest with partition keys, Lambda/Firehose/consumers, you do not SSH the broker. Replay only inside the retention you pay for.
cells.consistency: Per-shard sequence order. Shared GetRecords throughput versus enhanced fan-out. No Kafka consumer-group coordinator you operate. Iterator position is progress, not a SQL commit.
cells.latency: Standard GetRecords is poll-and-wait (often hundreds of ms). Enhanced fan-out lowers that tax. Not a sub-ms cache.
cells.scaling: Split/merge shards or on-demand mode. Classic provisioned planning: on the order of 1 MB/s or 1,000 records/s ingest per shard—measure the current account limits.
cells.failure: You do not tune ISR. Provisioned throttling, expired iterators after falling behind retention, regional impairment. No unclean-election knob; also no on-disk hexdump of your log.
cells.costOps: Shard-hour or on-demand plus PUT and extended retention. Default retention is 24 h unless you pay to extend (up to a long window the vendor names). Replay dies when retention dies.
cells.whenNot: You needed self-managed multi-week offset replay, Kafka-class consumer groups, or a log you restore from your own disks. TokenX money still belongs in a ledger, not a shard.

cells.workload: Primary already commits the business row. A few workers need at-least-once fan-out (notify, search, analytics) without a partitioned log product.
cells.consistency: Commit order of the source database. No independent consumer groups on a durable multi-reader log. CDC/outbox apply is a second boundary: at-least-once plus an idempotent sink.
cells.latency: Poll interval or CDC slot lag, often hundreds of ms to seconds, not ISR round-trip.
cells.scaling: One publisher until WAL/slot or poller CPU saturates. Many independent replayable consumers are why you add a log, not more threads on the same poller.
cells.failure: Poller crash delays fan-out; the ledger row remains. Dual-write without an outbox can commit money and lose the event, or the reverse. Replication slot fill can halt the primary.
cells.costOps: No broker cluster. You still own the publisher, the outbox table or CDC slot, idempotent sinks, and backpressure into the primary.
cells.whenNot: Partition parallelism, many independent groups, or replay measured in days. Do not skip the outbox and dual-write Kafka 'for speed.' TokenX ACK still waits on the ledger transaction, not on the poller.

assumptions: Kafka planning default: RF=3, acks=all, min.insync.replicas=2, producer idempotence, ISR-only leader election, finite retention. HW is the exclusive ISR read gate; LEO can sit ahead; KIP-101 truncates diverged followers by leader epoch.
Pulsar-class: brokers plus BookKeeper-class bookies; name ensemble, write quorum, and ack quorum per topic. Metadata is a separate authority.
Kinesis-class: managed shards, vendor AZ replication, retention you pay for (24 h unless extended). Throughput numbers are order-of-magnitude planning, not a named fleet SLO.
Outbox-only: business row and outbox row in one primary transaction; publisher is async. No claim that CDC is atomic with the sink.
All four classes deliver at-least-once to external sinks unless a named boundary (unique key, Kafka produce-plus-offset transaction, SQS FIFO queue-window dedup) is in force. None is TokenX money.
